title: The Cost of Necessity
source_note: Author-provided project text described as final canon-clean. Excerpts are sourced dramatic testimony; no museum machine invariant or observed mention edge is promoted into historical proof.
source_boundaries: AZURAVEL remains an independent constructed language. No canonical in-universe historical connection to Starsilk or official translation is asserted.
The cited Starsilk testimony is a user-authored narrative. Its content is not a machine-verified witness recording, location map, or coordinate set.
Starsilk_Character_Dossier project museum machine edges carry observed mentions only, not causal, personal, temporal, or affiliation claims.
Artwork is an interpretive diagram; no geolocation, adjacency, scale, or casualty count is inferred from the displayed marks.

cases.title: The memorial image
cases.root_reason: Memory is an AZ1 semantic analogy, not a Starsilk translation.

claim.label: OFFICIAL READING
claim.lead: A red circle around a dead world. The memorial images made it possible to point, classify, and move on.
claim.detail: Codec mapped the Blood Rings for approach vectors, blind corridors, and limits beyond which instruments lied. The maps made the ring operationally legible.

cost.label: WITNESS READING
cost.lead: The ring was made of the civilization that had lived below it.
cost.detail: In Codec's testimony, the orbital material came from homogenized cities and inhabitants: hatcheries, schools, hospitals, markets, and lovers. The Drakken's Blood Rings were not metaphorical halos. Their source was people.

cases.question: What did the legend make impossible to see?
cases.source_scope: Authorial testimony on Drakken Blood Rings; not a newly discovered artifact or an exact cartographic record.

cases.title: Containment efficiency
cases.root_reason: Star is an AZ1 lexical analogy; it does not encode a Starsilk Macro.

claim.label: COMMAND READING
claim.lead: Tiger stopped the Drakken advance. The Siege Wall held.
claim.detail: At the Aureal Gate, Drakken weaponization of Starsilk prompted Tiger's cold containment response. His heliocide collapsed successive stars and formed a black-hole lattice that contained Mother and her forces.

cost.label: WITNESS READING
cost.lead: Those locks had been inhabited suns.
cost.detail: Codec describes thousands of stars collapsing while civilian evacuation windows closed and distress pings became non-actionable. The containment succeeded and imposed catastrophic loss. Tactical success is not moral absolution.

cases.question: If a defensive structure is made of star systems, which part of it counts as a casualty?
cases.source_scope: Authorial testimony plus Starsilk active-canon locks; abstract structure, not a measured topology.

cases.title: Acceptable deformation
cases.root_reason: Effect is an AZ1 semantic analogy, not an official translation of a military term.

claim.label: AFTER-ACTION READING
claim.lead: A Pyric titan was stopped before it could sever an agricultural and refugee supply chain.
claim.detail: Codec selected and verified the Corpse-Burn Firewall Macro against the titan rooted in the geothermal nexus of Nacreous VI. The sector survived the immediate threat.

cost.label: PLANETARY READING
cost.lead: The strike left Nacreous VI a Level 3 remnant world.
cost.detail: Permanent storm shear, fixed mountain trauma, and damaged soil chemistry remained. The report's phrase acceptable planetary deformation names a result, not a restoration.

cases.question: When survival is verified, who certifies the cost?
cases.source_scope: Authorial testimony; named operation and damage are source-grounded. Illustration is schematic.

cases.title: The oldest mask
cases.root_reason: Necessity is an AZ1 lexical analogy; it neither translates nor excuses Codec's words.
cases.primary_evidence: I became necessary. That is not the same thing.

claim.label: THE REFUGEE'S READING
claim.lead: The Drakken were contained. The sector lived. The actions worked.
claim.detail: A young refugee calls Tiger a savior, then calls Codec a savior. Codec agrees with the prevented losses, not with the moral conclusion drawn from them.

cost.label: CODEC'S READING
cost.lead: Being necessary and being good are not interchangeable states.
cost.detail: Codec recounts how the Administration became efficient at selecting sacrificed worlds. His critique includes himself: he chose the wound, verified the strike, and lived with its consequence. Necessity cannot be allowed to erase responsibility.

cases.question: What must a ledger refuse to subtract?
cases.source_scope: Authorial dialogue and the canon-locked distinction between Codec's care, coercion, and moral compromise.
